newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns Baa1 to HK$2 bln FRCD of BOC, HK.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns Baa1 to HK$2 bln FRCD of BOC, HK.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it has assigned Baa1 rating to HK$2 billion floating rate certificates of deposit (FRCD) of Bank of China, Hong Kong branch.

The agency said the rating reflected the importance of the bank's business franchises in China and Hong Kong, as well as its weak financial condition, with low profitablitly and poor asset quality which undermined its reported capital base.

The rating also included the likelihood that the bank would continue to be supported by the substantial resoucres of China's central government during the current period of financial and economic reform, although the predictability of this support was tempered by the long-term intention of the government to place the state banks onto a commerical basis, Moody's said.

The agency currently rates the bank Baa1 for its senior long-term cross-border foreign currency debt, and Baa2/Prime-3 for its long- and short-term non-resident foreign currency deposits. Its financial strength rating is D.
The Bank of China, headquartered in Beijing, is the second largest bank in China, and reported total assets of 2.27 trillion yuan at the end of 1995.
